notes: הַנָּבִיא הַהוּא and הַחוֹלֵם ... הַהוּא are read under rule 41's closing paragraph, on the model of שֵׁם הַמָּקוֹם הַהוּא: the demonstrative pronoun takes the written *that*, both articles of each phrase go unrepresented, and the construct דִּבְרֵי takes a supplied *the* of its own.

A competing reading would front the *the* of *the words* onto the article of נָבִיא under rule 29; that is rejected because a determiner already stands before the rectum's own word, so nothing is fronted.

הֲיִשְׁכֶם אֹהֲבִים → *whether ye love* follows rule 50's אִיתֵיכוֹן פָלְחִין → *ye serve* precedent: הֲ takes the written *whether*, the existential יֵשׁ is unrepresented because the ASV writes no separate frame, and its suffix takes the subject pronoun *ye*.
